commits.message: installed AI clients as the model of a local runtime, first-start setup as a wizard
commits.body:
A runtime that runs alone can think through an AI client installed on the
machine, on the person's own subscription. Four clients are supported; each
runs headless as a model for the text classes, gets a step's tools over MCP
for the length of the call, and validates structured output itself where it
can.

- harness/: detection (version, sign-in), a per-client environment taken
  from the login shell with the subscription sign-in first, the headless
  calls, and the sign-in in a pseudo-terminal the studio shows inline
- mcp/bridge: a call's tools served over MCP; they run in the tenant
  context of the call that opened the bridge
- first start: the dev-login page is skipped where it is the only way in;
  the setup stays in front until a test call has worked on the chosen
  source. It opens with the choices alone, then shows what the choice needs
  (sign-in, keys, test) with colour-coded steps, a host per choice, a footer
  line and a layout for narrow screens
- language switch (EN/DE) in the setup and the user menu, applied in place
- settings: the source picker lists the installed clients; parts whose
  service is not there yet stay behind feature flags
- desktop bundle: the pty helper keeps its execute bit

commits.message: a database per tenant, model classes, sign-in at the Manage-App, phone inputs

footers.value:
every tenant has its own libSQL database behind withTenant(); a control database
maps public links and run ids to their tenant and counts across tenants. tenant_id replaces
owner_id. Files live under the tenant's prefix, in the data folder or an S3 bucket.

Two ways to run: alone (one-time link, Host and Origin check, own keys, Ollama or a linked
account) and managed (MANAGE_URL: OIDC sign-in, tokens verified against the Manage-App's
JWKS, model calls through its gateway). Accounts, credits and Stripe left this repo.

Steps name a model class (classifier, standard, high, highest, image, video, audio) and an
effort hint. Cost per step is recorded; a run is estimated before it starts and its credits
are reserved.

publish a local wizard to the cloud through the import API, studio chat on the Claude
subscription, sandbox engines behind one interface (Docker, agentOS), a cloud compose file
with a separate Chromium container, FSL-1.1-MIT.

camera with several shots and clips, code scan, location, voice notes, signature,
share sheet, wake lock, per-wizard home-screen entry, and the damage-report starter.

owner_id. Files live under the tenant's prefix, in the data folder or an S3 bucket.

Two ways to run: alone (one-time link, Host and Origin check, own keys, Ollama or a linked
account) and managed (MANAGE_URL: OIDC sign-in, tokens verified against the Manage-App's
JWKS, model calls through its gateway). Accounts, credits and Stripe left this repo.

Steps name a model class (classifier, standard, high, highest, image, video, audio) and an

commits.message: interactive widgets with a workspace per wizard, shareable results
commits.body:
Widgets are HTML apps written once into the wizard's workspace; a widget
step only binds each run's data into them — no model call, same look
every run. The result is one self-contained HTML file (scripts, styles,
images and reference data inlined) that previews, downloads and renders
to PNG, PDF and MP4 (the widget's timeline stepped frame by frame in
Chromium, encoded with ffmpeg). Widgets talk to the platform through
window.wizard: data, brand, workspace files, ready(), timeline().

Workspace files live in a content-addressed blob store; publishing and
every run snapshot the file list, so later edits never change a running
or shared result. The studio gets a Files tab and a widget inspector
with a live preview from sample data; agent steps can read the
workspace; MCP clients get list/read/write/delete_file and check_widget.

Generated HTML may run scripts, but only in an opaque origin with no
network: previews are sandboxed frames mounted once their HTML is
there, a CSP blocks every request, renders run in an offline browser
context, and the runtime re-fires resize for frames that get their
size late.

The architect is now a Mastra agent with tools: it edits the wizard
through the same ops as MCP, writes workspace files, downloads
reference data in one batch, reshapes it with run_script in an offline
browser, and checks the widget with a screenshot. The chat shows what
it is doing and says so when it runs out of steps.

Finished runs can be shared as /s/<token>: deliverables and downloads
only, never the answers, with a link to make your own. The share sheet
offers link, e-mail, X, LinkedIn, WhatsApp, Facebook and the phone's
share menu; shared links get an Open Graph image. Runs of end users
without an account expire after RESULT_TTL_DAYS (7) and are purged
hourly.

commits.message: live studio — MCP and other edits show up without a reload
commits.body:
The editor subscribes to /api/studio/wizards/:id/stream. Every draft
write (studio, architect, MCP client) announces its revision and the
steps it touched; the editor fetches the new state, the changed steps
pulse in the diagram and the header names the client. Notes left by an
MCP client appear in the thread between turns.

Inspector edits still unsaved when another write lands are never lost:
their save meets the newer revision, the edits merge step by step onto
it (studio wins on the same step) and save again.

commits.message: OAuth sign-in for MCP clients, connected apps in settings
commits.body:
MCP clients connect without a key: they discover /api/mcp (RFC 9728),
register themselves (dynamic registration or a client metadata
document), the admin signs in and allows access on /consent, and the
client gets a token bound to /api/mcp. Tools follow the granted scopes.
Settings list connected apps; disconnecting removes the consent and the
tokens and cuts the app off at once. Personal API keys keep working.

Registrations with only loopback or custom-scheme redirects count as
native apps, so clients that leave application_type out still connect.

Includes migration 0002 of the workspace work, which 0003 builds on.

commits.message: MCP endpoint for authoring wizards with personal API keys
commits.body:
Admins build and change wizards from their own MCP clients. /api/mcp
(stateless Streamable HTTP, official SDK v2) offers 14 tools: authoring
guide, starters, projects, wizards, validate, create, edit ops, replace,
publish, sharing, test runs with answers, run reports with signed
download links. Personal API keys in Settings, rate-limited per key.

One service layer serves the studio routes and the MCP tools. Draft
writes carry a revision and refuse stale ones. MCP notes show up in the
studio thread. The architect and the MCP guide share one authoring text.
Architect turns that fail no longer leave their message behind; the
document preview frame renders again.
